items.stem: In a planner-worker-reviewer design, what is the reviewer agent's main purpose?

options.text: To check and critique the workers' outputs before they are accepted
options.rationale: Correct: the reviewer/critic validates results, improving reliability.

options.text: To generate the original task plan
options.rationale: That is the planner's role, not the reviewer's.

options.text: To execute all the tool calls
options.rationale: Workers carry out the work; the reviewer evaluates it.
That is unrelated to the reviewer role.

items.explanation: Correct: the reviewer/critic validates results, improving reliability.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are genuine risks of adding more agents to a system? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Higher token cost and latency from extra communication
options.rationale: Correct: each agent interaction adds calls, cost and delay.

options.text: Agents can loop or amplify each other's errors
options.rationale: Correct: poorly bounded agent dialogue can loop or compound mistakes.

options.text: It guarantees higher accuracy on every task
options.rationale: Multi-agent designs do not guarantee better accuracy.

options.text: It removes the need to evaluate the system
options.rationale: Evaluation is still required, arguably more so.

items.explanation: Correct: each agent interaction adds calls, cost and delay.

items.stem: Two worker agents return contradictory answers. Which mechanism most directly resolves this?

options.text: A defined conflict-resolution step such as a reviewer or majority vote
options.rationale: Correct: an explicit resolution/voting step decides between conflicting outputs.
Removing state loses information needed to resolve the conflict.

options.text: Letting both answers pass through unresolved
options.rationale: Passing contradictions downstream propagates the conflict.

items.explanation: Correct: an explicit resolution/voting step decides between conflicting outputs.
